headline: City Resident Successfully Transitions To Living Entirely Inside Elevators During Morning Peak Hour
body:
A resident of a high-rise apartment complex in South Bengaluru has successfully completed a transition to living full-time inside the building’s lift during morning peak hours to ensure he actually reaches his office on time. By moving his workstation, a folding chair, and a mobile hotspot into the elevator car at 7:45 AM, the resident has bypassed the traditional 45-minute wait time caused by the building's maintenance-starved mechanical system.

“I’ve essentially turned the lift into my personal studio apartment with vertical mobility,” said the resident, who now conducts his daily Zoom meetings while suspended between the 14th and 19th floors. “The neighbors were initially annoyed when I hung a whiteboard on the control panel, but they quickly realized that if I stay inside, the elevator makes fewer stops at residential floors, which actually speeds up their own commute.”

Building management has reportedly welcomed the development, noting that the presence of a human occupant allows them to justify the elevator’s perpetual ‘In-Service’ status despite a faulty motor. The resident plans to expand his living quarters next month by installing a small solar-powered coffee machine in the corner, provided the elevator remains stuck between the 8th and 9th floors long enough for a courier to slide a delivery through the door gap.
caption: Work-from-home takes a vertical turn as one man reclaims his commute. #UrbanLiving #BengaluruLife #RealEstateReality #OfficeLife
